# AbstractCode

> An agentic coding assistant with two clients — a Rust terminal application
> (`tui/`, crates.io `abstractcode`) and a TypeScript browser application
> (`web/`, npm `@abstractframework/code`). Neither runs the coding agent: it
> runs durably on AbstractGateway, and both clients observe and steer it over
> HTTP and SSE. A session is portable between them.

This file follows the `llms.txt` manifest format (curated links). Use `llms.txt`
when you can fetch the linked files, and `llms-full.txt` when you need one
offline snapshot of the documentation. Format reference: https://llmstxt.org/

Ground rules for reading this repository:

- Status: **pre-alpha**. Interfaces and behavior may change between releases.
- The source of truth is the code, and the executable invariants are the tests
  (`cargo test --workspace` for the terminal client, `npm test` in `web/` for
  the browser client). If the documentation and the code disagree, follow the
  code.
- The two clients release independently: tag `v<version>` publishes the crate,
  tag `web-v<version>` publishes the npm package.
- A reachable AbstractGateway is required. There is no standalone mode.
  Archiving conversations, the Archived · N lists and the gateway's default
  voice routes need AbstractGateway 0.13.0 or later; the browser client 0.15.0
  (shared unread markers, the Avatar view's live line and Findings, the Paused · N
  section) needs 0.20.0 or later; `@` mentions and the reply's author (terminal
  0.15.0, browser 0.16.0) need 0.21.0.
- Tools are approval-gated by default; approvals are durable gateway commands,
  so a wait raised in one client is answerable from the other.
- The authoritative command list is `/help` inside the terminal client, and
  `abstractcode --help` for the command line.

## Browser navigation

Open **Model** directly from the right-hand icon rail to change the selected conversation or automation’s model. **Agent** groups workflow, tools and skills; **Workspace** controls folders. **Voice** configures this app’s speech and devices. Automation Model panels show **Limits**; conversation panels show **Limits & streaming**. The Docs assistant’s speaker reads a reply aloud when speech is configured.

Type `@` in the message box and pick an entity to mention it. The list starts with the conversation's agent: a message to entities only does not reach the agent (no agent run), and with the agent picked too your message starts the agent's turn (the agent answers only the part meant for it, or says nothing). Then each picked entity reads the conversation's history and answers in turn under its own name (while its answer is on its way, a bubble with its name and moving dots stands in its place), and every reply says who wrote it. Your sent message keeps its chips; in the browser, a chip shows the entity's card on hover. If an entity cannot answer, the message comes back with only the entities that did not answer; send it again unchanged to ask only those. See [mentioning an entity](docs/getting-started.md#mentioning-an-entity).

The terminal client supports source-aware assistant text/table/code selection.
Explain, Use as context and Change stage quoted content into an existing draft;
sending remains explicit. See [terminal selection](tui/docs/api.md#selected-content).

## Project documentation

- [README](README.md): what AbstractCode is, the two clients, and a quick start
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): running a gateway, installing a client, credentials, first run, mentioning an entity with `@` (in both clients)
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): the clients, the browser app server, the gateway, the terminal's voice bridge, the run stream with live reply deltas, attention from your event stream (`/me/events` catch-up + SSE: the terminal chip and the browser badge, "N waiting for you · M new"), the thin-client contract, and repository layout
- [API and integration points](docs/api.md): the command-line surface, the library surface, and the gateway contract (runs, streams, your event stream, entities and `@` mentions with the turn `author`, discovery, workspace files, conversations and archiving, automations, voice, about)
- [Workflows](docs/workflows.md): the gateway default agent workflow, selecting a workflow, and the `abstractcode.agent.v1` interface
- [Automations](docs/automations.md): Repeat, Daily, Weekly, Monthly and Once schedules on the account's time zone (the gateway words each rule and computes each next run); configurable growing-context budgets and result email; creating, managing, answering and discussing gateway automations from the terminal (`/automations`, `/automation`, Edit in `/settings`) and the browser (the Automations sidebar section)
- [Interface events](docs/ui_events.md): the workflow-driven event contract
- [FAQ](docs/faq.md): recurring questions and current limitations
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): symptom-oriented diagnosis and fixes, including archive and voice on an older gateway
- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): the full documentation map

## Terminal client

- [Terminal client README](tui/README.md): features, interface tour, keys, themes
- [Terminal getting started](tui/docs/getting-started.md): terminal-specific setup
- [Terminal API](tui/docs/api.md): command-line options, slash commands (`/settings`, `/activity`, `/sessions`, `/archive`, `/automations`, `/workflow`, `/files`, `/stream`, `/docs`, `/about`, `/model`, `/mtp`, `/voice`, `/speak`, `/dictate`, …), keys, the settings panels (bound to the conversation or an automation's definition, revisions), the Workspaces chooser and the command sandbox lines, streamed replies, voice (gateway routes, host audio via AbstractVoice), exit codes
- [Terminal architecture](tui/docs/architecture.md): how the client is built on AbstractTUI — threads, the ledger fold, live replies
- [Terminal troubleshooting](tui/docs/troubleshooting.md): terminal, rendering, and connection problems
- [Terminal FAQ](tui/docs/faq.md): durability, workspaces, tokens, steering semantics, voice (which Python, Gateway default, microphone permission)
- [Orchestration cards](tui/docs/orchestration-cards.md): the coding workflows accepted by `--workflow` and when to choose each

## Browser client

- [Browser client README](web/README.md): running it, configuration, credential handling
- [Web overview](docs/web.md): the right rail (Activity, Files with the shared file viewer and audio waveform player, and the settings panels Model, Workflow, Workspace, Tools, Skills, Voice bound to the selected conversation or automation — an automation change saves a new revision), the Archived · N line with Unarchive at the end of each sidebar list, archiving a conversation from its card or header ⋯ (inline confirm, never a delete), the shared About, standard header widgets, workflow selection, conversation files and generated outputs, responsive desktop/tablet/phone navigation, touch and keyboard controls, the two stacking Automations / Conversations drawers with `Oct 2 · 2 turns · 7 tools` conversation cards and two-line automation cards (Active switch), the automation header (Run now, Stop, Edit, Archive), the Voice panel (gateway default routes, output and input devices with Tests) and composer dictation, streamed replies, approvals, and workspace policy
- [Web deployment](docs/deployment-web.md): hosting it behind HTTPS, reverse proxies, forwarded client addresses
- [iPhone notes](docs/deployment-iphone.md): Safari and progressive web app behavior, and how the interface adapts to the phone
